title: AgentConfig
description: Portable agent manifest (schema_version 2). A single snake_case JSON document that fully describes an agent: prompt, model strategy, runtime limits, memory, retrieval, tools, and guardrails. The same document may be stored by a control plane, checked into source control, or handed to an on-device runtime. Deployment topology, tenant identity, and provider API keys are outside the manifest: keys are always runtime-supplied and never appear in the artifact. Validators MUST accept unknown members (forward compatibility) and tooling MUST preserve them when loading, validating, or repackaging a manifest.

version.description: Version label of this agent configuration (e.g. "v2"). Chosen by the author or publishing control plane; not the schema version.

schema_version.description: Version of this manifest schema. This document describes schema_version "2".

AgentRuntimeConfig.description: Execution limits for the agent loop.

streaming.description: Whether the runtime should stream responses.

max_turns.description: Maximum agent-loop turns per request. Null or absent means runtime default.

max_concurrent_tools.description: Maximum tool calls executed concurrently. Null or absent means runtime default.

AgentModelCandidate.description: One model the agent may run on, as "provider:model" (e.g. "openai:gpt-4o", "anthropic:claude-sonnet-5", "apple:foundation-models").

name.description: Candidate name, unique within the manifest (e.g. "primary").

model.description: Model reference in "provider:model" form. The runtime resolves the provider; keys are supplied at runtime, never in the manifest.

strategy.description: How the runtime picks among candidates (e.g. "single", "weighted", "fallback"). Runtimes treat unrecognized strategies as pass-through and may reject them at execution time.

candidates.description: Candidate models the strategy selects from.

routing_policy.description: Strategy-specific routing options (e.g. {"sticky": true}). Pass-through metadata for the runtime.

type.description: Memory implementation (e.g. "buffer"). Null or absent means runtime default.

window_turns.description: How many turns the memory window retains.

enabled.description: Whether retrieval is active for this agent.

corpus_ids.description: Corpora to search. Identifiers are runtime-defined.

filters.description: Retrieval filters (arbitrary JSON). Pass-through metadata for the runtime.

ToolEndpoint.description: Optional HTTP execution endpoint for a tool. Tools without an endpoint are executed natively by the runtime or the host app.

url.description: Endpoint URL the runtime calls with the tool arguments.

method.description: HTTP method. Defaults to POST when absent.

headers.description: Static headers sent with each call. Secrets should be injected at runtime rather than stored here.

ToolDefinition.description: An LLM-native tool schema, plus an optional execution endpoint.

description.description: What the tool does, written for the model.

parameters.description: JSON Schema object describing the tool's arguments.

endpoint.description: Optional HTTP endpoint that executes the tool.

require_user_confirmation.description: Tool names that must be confirmed by the user before executing.

max_total_runtime_ms.description: Total tool-execution budget per turn, in milliseconds.

max_tools_per_turn.description: Maximum number of tool calls per turn.

AgentToolsConfig.description: Tool surface for the agent. `allowed` absent means no allow-list is declared; `allowed: []` is an explicit allow-list enabling no tools. A manifest may carry definitions without an allow-list; consumers apply their own normalization rather than inferring hidden built-in tools.

definitions.description: Tool schemas available to the agent.

tool_policy.description: Execution constraints applied across all tools.

AgentOutputFormat.description: One per-turn response format. Mirrors the Anthropic Messages API output_config.format shape so runtimes can pass it through or map it to provider-native guided generation.

type.description: Format discriminator. "json_schema" constrains each assistant turn's final payload to the declared JSON Schema.

schema.description: JSON Schema object the assistant turn's structured payload must conform to.

AgentOutputConfig.description: Per-turn structured output declaration. Absent means unstructured text output (default behavior).

AgentGuardrailsConfig.description: Safety and content policy switches. Semantics are runtime-defined; unknown members are pass-through.

pii_redaction.description: Whether the runtime should redact PII.

jailbreak_detection.description: Whether the runtime should screen for jailbreak attempts.

blocked_topics.description: Topics the agent must refuse to engage with.
